label: Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) — 2-compartment IV
_note: Every entry with enabled=true in baseline/iiv/effects comes from a file inside this repository.
Entries with enabled=false have their structure implemented but no sourced coefficient yet; they
stay out of the computation until a value is filled in. covmodel.assertSourced() enforces this.

_sourceConflict.note: Two files record the same model (DOI 10.1007/s10928-017-9528-y, N=2195) with different numbers. Needs confirmation.
_sourceConflict.choiceMadeHere: The curated values, to stay consistent with CURATED.pembrolizumab in index.html

_papers.note: What the four Keytruda papers supplied by the user contain from a covariate standpoint. Page numbers follow pdfplumber.

22_Tomoko_2017 (Freshwater, J Immunother.role: Most useful. Justifies the fixed 200 mg Q3W dose by citing a popPK model.

coefficientsConfirmed.remark: These match CL_WT 0.578 / VC_WT 0.492 in extracted_poppk_params.csv exactly, confirming that the simulator's Keytruda model descends from this lineage

22_Tomoko_2017 (Freshwater, J Immunother.newlyIncorporated: Q and Vp are also weight-adjusted, with the same exponents as CL and Vc respectively (p3). This was missing from the existing model and has been added as Q_WT / VP_WT.
22_Tomoko_2017 (Freshwater, J Immunother.weightDistribution: median 77.2 kg, range 35.7-209.5 kg — p4 (reflected in the population block)
22_Tomoko_2017 (Freshwater, J Immunother.namedButWithoutCoefficients: sex, baseline eGFR, baseline albumin, prior ipilimumab, cancer type, baseline ECOG PS — all stated only as 'retained in the popPK model as identified in [4]' with no values given (p3)
22_Tomoko_2017 (Freshwater, J Immunother.negativeFinding: Clearance did not differ meaningfully across cancer types (p5)

21_Longoria_2016.role: Review / label summary. No popPK table.
21_Longoria_2016.valuesConfirmed: CL geometric mean 0.2 L/day (CV 37%), terminal half-life 27 days (CV 38%), accumulation 2.2-fold, steady state by 19 weeks — p4
negativeFindings: 'Age (range 15-94 years), gender, race, and tumor burden were found to have no clinically important effect on clearance.' — p4

'Patients with mild (GFR 60-90, n=937) or moderate (GFR 30-60, n=201) renal impairment have no clinically important difference in clearance compared to patients with normal renal function (GFR >=90, n=1027).' — p4
21_Longoria_2016.implication: On this evidence there is no reason to add tumor burden, age, race or renal function as covariates. Sex is called not clinically important, yet a coefficient does exist in the model — meaning the effect size is small.

20_Shimizu_2016.role: Phase 1 in Japanese patients with advanced solid tumors. NCA, not popPK.
20_Shimizu_2016.covariates: None. Covariate analysis is impossible at n=10. ADA was not detected.
20_Shimizu_2016.usefulness: Only as external validity — checking whether the Japanese subgroup falls within the model's predicted range.

30_Hutchins_2020.covariates: None. Unrelated to the human covariate model.
30_Hutchins_2020.remark: The +- signs in the CL table are broken into (cid:5), which hampers automated extraction.

_papers.conclusion: Only two covariates can be newly enabled from these four papers: Q_WT and VP_WT. For the rest (albumin, sex, eGFR, ECOG, cancer type, IPI) Tomoko lists the names but gives no coefficients, so obtaining them requires reference [4], Ahamadi M et al. 'Model-based characterization of the pharmacokinetics of pembrolizumab' (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2017).

reportedChecks.source: 21_Longoria_2016.pdf p4 — 'the terminal half-life is 27 days (CV: 38%)'. The source gives a CV rather than a CI, so the interval is set arbitrarily at about +-20% (the pass/fail mark is indicative only).
21_Longoria_2016.pdf p4 — 'the systemic accumulation is 2.2-fold' (Q3W repeat dosing). No CI in the source; +-10% assumed.

regressionCheck.source: docs/tracker.md 2026-07-21 — 'Cmax 103, Ctrough 38 (consistent with clinical data)'. Condition: the app's default screen, whose sex select defaults to Female.

bandNote.fixed: Under this setting the band matches the width of the 90% prediction intervals in FDA Table 5 to within 0.87~1.15-fold.
bandNote.sampled: Under this setting the shaded band widens 1.1~1.4-fold and the median rises by 5~8% — the intervals in FDA Table 5 appear to reflect IIV only, with covariates fixed at their medians. Turn this option off when comparing with the source.
bandNote.source: Measured for the pembrolizumab specs in this repository (covariate/analysis.js output). It says nothing about any other drug, which is why it lives in the spec.

effects.desc: Body-weight power model, the standard form for mAb allometry.

effects.source: 22_Tomoko_2017.pdf p3 — 'Two additional parameters (Q and V_P) ... were also adjusted for WT, using the same values for the exponents as for CL and Vc, respectively.'
effects.desc: Q takes the same exponent as CL (0.578). The previous model applied no weight scaling to Q — an omission relative to what the paper states.

effects.source: 22_Tomoko_2017.pdf p3 — same sentence. Vp takes the same exponent as Vc (0.492).
effects.desc: Vp takes the same exponent as Vc. The previous model applied no weight scaling to Vp.
effects.corroboration: The third pembrolizumab model in data/PPKPARAMETER.csv (DOI 10.1016/j.xphs.2018.10.064) reports VP_WT 0.543 / Q_WT 0.555 — the same pattern (VP close to the VC exponent, Q close to the CL exponent).

effects.desc: The largest exponent on CL in this model. Lower albumin raises CL (a proxy for catabolic state).
CL is 15.2% lower in females. Kept in the (1+coef) form used by CURATED in index.html.

desc: Time-varying CL. All 3 pembrolizumab models in PPKPARAMETER.csv have 'Time dependency'=0, whereas
in the same library 5 of 7 nivolumab models, as well as durvalumab, avelumab and toripalimab, have =1.
docs/PRD.md listed 'time-dependent CL' as a non-goal, so the engine did not support it at all.
The structure (sigmoid Emax / exponential) is implemented in covmodel.js; only the coefficients are missing.
With Emax<0, CL decreases over time; T50 is the time (days) to reach half of that change.

population._note: Covariate distributions for the virtual population. These are assumptions rather than observed data and are labelled as such in the report.

WT.source: 22_Tomoko_2017.pdf p4 — '...distribution of body weight, with a median of 77.2 kg and a range of 35.7-209.5 kg' (weight distribution of the virtual patients sampled from the popPK analysis population)
WT.cvDerivation: DERIVED — the paper gives only a median and a range, no SD or CV. Assuming log-normality and treating the reported min/max as roughly +-3.3 SD at N~2195 gives sigma~0.268, i.e. CV~27%. The min/max are used directly as clamps. The CV therefore carries an assumption.

ALB.source: ASSUMPTION — the mean is the model's reference albumin of 39.6 g/L; SD 4.5 is assumed.

SEX.source: ASSUMPTION — a female fraction of 40% is assumed.

iv.source: The only route studied: 200 mg every 3 weeks as a 30-minute infusion.

sc.source: No absorption rate or bioavailability for pembrolizumab exists anywhere in this repository. A subcutaneous pembrolizumab product was approved in 2025 (with berahyaluronidase alfa); adding it here needs that product's own population PK source.

regimen.source: data/regimen.csv — pembrolizumab 200 mg q21day IV, 0.5 h infusion (approved regimen)

residualError.source: UNSOURCED — data/extracted_poppk_params.csv, the source of this spec, records no residual error for pembrolizumab.
